title: ATV offers to buy Northern Songs shares | 1969
content:
On 28 March 1969, Dick James and Lew Grade met to discuss the sale of James’s shares in Northern Songs to Grade’s media company Associated Television (ATV). On 11 April a formal offer was made.

Grade offered James and Silver 37 shillings per share – for a total of £1,525,000 – to acquire 1,604,750 shares in Northern Songs, in addition to the 137,000 that ATV already owned. The total would give ATV almost 35% of the company.

The offer was made on this day to the company shareholders by Warburg & Co, acting on behalf of ATV. The Beatles made a counter offer on 20 April, but ultimately lost control of Northern Songs in September 1969.
